annotation.title_clean: Application of the General Data Protection Regulation on Household Social Robots
annotation.title_en: Application of the General Data Protection Regulation on Household Social Robots
annotation.venue: University of Szeged, Doctoral School of Law
annotation.summary_en: Doctoral dissertation analysing how the GDPR applies to household social robots, using scenarios, design fiction and expert interviews. It examines personal data, profiling, automated decision-making, controller and joint-controller roles, legal bases and consent, transparency, the household exemption and vulnerable users, and considers whether GDPR needs updating.
key_provisions_or_claims: Household social robots raise GDPR challenges around profiling, automated decision-making and unpredictable learning behaviour.
Users may qualify as joint controllers, narrowing the household exemption in some cases.
Consent and transparency (meaningful, intelligible information) are difficult to meet, especially for vulnerable groups.
Controller, joint controller and processor roles need clearer allocation to assign liability.
Scenario-based expert interviews assess whether GDPR rules need updating.
